Druid · Meta

Storm Shred Druid

werewolf melee / storm hybrid

Druid meta adjusted werewolf melee / storm hybrid PTR

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 15 (PTR)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The Season 14 Storm Shred Druid read forward onto the 3.2.0 PTR, and this page has to open with the bad news because it is the whole story. 3.2.0 guts Storm Shepherd's Call from roughly a 1.2 million percent multiplier to 80%, and cuts Might of the Ursine from 13% to 4%. Storm Shepherd's Call is the entire reason Season 14's Shred Druid existed: it is what made Spirit regeneration scale damage and inverted the build's whole gearing logic. Removing it does not adjust this build, it retires the archetype - the digest says so in those words - and the +30% Druid core stat scalar (1.25 to 1.625) does not begin to compensate, because a baseline additive buff cannot replace a gutted multiplier. Both 3.2.0 class tier reads agree Druid is among the losers of the patch, though they disagree by a tier on how far it falls (aoeah B, mtmmo C). So why is this page here? Because the owner's requirement is that every class carries a build, and the honest options were this or nothing: no 3.2.0 build guide exists on any major English site, no 3.2.0 skill allocation or paragon ordering is published for any class, and inventing a replacement Druid build would be fabrication rather than research. This is therefore the Season 14 build with its Season 14 numbers, carried forward with its own obituary attached. Use it to understand what the Druid was and what the patch takes away; do not read it as a recommendation for 3.2.0. When Season 15 ships, expect this file to be rebuilt around a different skill entirely rather than re-tuned. Two Season 14 caveats also carry forward: survivability is the Druid's named weakness, and Maxroll attributed part of Storm Shepherd's Season 14 dominance to bugs - including that clicking Shred beat holding it - which is context for why the multiplier was cut this hard.

Requirements

  • Tibault's Willpants
  • Ifeh's Dire Totemoffhand
  • Waxing Gibbousweapon
  • Malefic Crescentamulet
  • Dirge of Airidahring 2
  • Gathlen's Birthrighthelm
  • Dark Howlgloves
  • Penitent Greavesboots
Stage
Move on when[ptr] Reach the point where you can equip a Berú of the Red Wolf Moon, the documented stand-in until Berú of the Storm Shepherd drops. On the PTR, Mrak simply hands you the gear.
Move on when[ptr] Berú of the Storm Shepherd equipped. In Season 14 this was the moment the build began - after it, the Spirit-regeneration-scales-damage rule took over and the entire affix priority changed. On the 3.2.0 PTR that rule is what has been cut from roughly 1.2 million percent to 80%, so expect the transition to be barely noticeable rather than transformative.
Move on when[ptr] In Season 14 this was a gear-tuning gate rather than a rotation change - full Mythic priority list and masterworking. It carries forward unchanged because 3.2.0 publishes nothing that would move it.

Skill point priority

  1. [ptr] Season 14 route read forward - 3.2.0 publishes no levelling guidance for any class
  2. Shred to max, using the Roundhouse variant while levelling
  3. Wind Shear for Spirit generation: you have no regeneration gear yet, so you need the basic skill
  4. Rabies as a levelling damage-over-time filler
  5. Cyclone Armor for the damage reduction the Druid badly needs early
  6. Debilitating Roar for survivability, Grizzly Rage as the ultimate

4Wolves

Rotation

Toggle Lightning Storm and Hurricane on, enter Grizzly Rage whenever available, refresh Debilitating Roar before it expires, then click Shred as fast as you can - do not hold the button, because rapid casts let Waxing Gibbous's extra attacks re-trigger the set bonus. [ptr] Note that this click-don't-hold interaction is one of the behaviours Maxroll described as a bug in Season 14, and 3.2.0's cut to Storm Shepherd's Call is the patch responding to that whole package.

  1. Shred maxed

  3. Lightning Storm kept mainly as the trigger for Aspect of the Orange Herald rather than for its own damage
  4. Grizzly Rage maxed for the damage multiplier

  6. Earthen Bulwark via the Que rune for the Barrier and Unstoppable

Board & glyph focus

[ptr] Rush the Legendary Nodes first, then expand into glyph areas. Season 14 glyph order: Spirit, Keeper, Fang and Claw, Earth and Sky, Fulminate - level each to its Legendary Bonus in that order, then evenly. Spirit Boons: Prickleskin on Deer, Scythe Talons or Avian Wrath on Eagle, Calamity on Wolf, Overload or Calm Before the Storm on Bonded Snake. None of this is re-measured for 3.2.0.

How to run them

[ptr] Carried over from Season 14 unchanged, which is sourced rather than assumed: mercenaries are not mentioned anywhere in the official 3.2.0 notes, so the Season 14 pairings are the only guidance that exists. The Season 14 reasoning: every one of the guide's profiles hires Raheir and takes Ground Slam, Bastion, Iron Wolf's Virtue and Raheir's Aegis - what you are buying is Valiance, a rotating cheat-death, and this build needs it because survivability is the acknowledged Druid weakness. Varyana reinforces on Bloodthirst for attack speed, which on a build whose damage came from clicking Shred as fast as possible was a direct damage gain. Icy Veins takes the other branch and reinforces with Aldkin on Field of Languish for damage reduction instead; take Aldkin if you are dying.

Uniques & where to find them

Tibault's Willpants

[ptr] On the PTR, take it from the vendor Mrak beside the main Waypoint: his PTR Boosts hand out uniques, maxed aspects, all runes, glyphs, level 70 and the seasonal items outright, so farming is not the test here. Expected live route, carried forward from Season 14: No dedicated boss - it sits in the General Unique Pool, so farm it via the Horadric Cube: Common pants plus Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique. 3.2.0 changes no boss loot table, but it does rework Mythic crafting into three routes -- the Horadric Cube's deterministic 'Upgrade Direct Item to Mythic' (which carries the Crafted tag), Jeweler rune crafting with a chosen slot and no Crafted tag, and the Blacksmith Mythic cache -- so the one-Crafted-Mythic cap stops being the binding constraint. Re-verify at launch.

Skill rotation

  1. Toggle Lightning Storm and Hurricane on, enter Grizzly Rage whenever it is available, refresh Debilitating Roar before it expires, then click Shred as fast as you can - never hold the button.
  2. Watch Cyclone Armor uptime and Grizzly Rage windows as the tiers climb.
